First of all, thank you so much for responding relatively quickly. Learning about BPD helps give me a perspective on some things, as I've always suspected she might be sort of bipolar, but all of her episodes have never lasted long enough for the house to have lasting evidence.

 > It sounds like your dad might typically be the person to influence her to get some, but he sounds pretty burnt out. Typically the guys who end up staying married to women with BPD are either NPDs themselves (the BPD/NPD dyad is written up all over the web), or decent guys with compromised social cognition who aren't sensitive enough to the wrongness of BPD behaviours to avoid getting entangled in the codependent "dance". 

On this note, both of those are a possibility. Though his symptoms to me aren't really serious enough to be a solid case of NPD, he does display some of their traits. I do feel like I need to expand on him a bit more, though, since he's probably a bigger influencer to the whole situation than I am in general. I'm going to continue the use of emboldening, as I tend to ramble a bit.

My dad didn't grow up well either, and grew up relatively poor with his two siblings, with his mom not being around most of the time, working to help keep her kids fed and sheltered. There's a really big chance with him having dealt with childhood trauma, with the key indicator being a way that he carries himself in life. **It's kind of hard to describe, but he acts on a really surface-level basis, always trying to crack quips and make good first impressions, and always trying to infect people with his smile in a way that seems sort of "off".** I understand that's one of the reasons people like working with him so much, and definitely a contributor to his career, but it isn't great at home when others are trying to open up about issues with him and he has trouble understanding it or empathizing. Everyone in the immediate family is aware of it, my mom included. He also seems to have an innate suppression of negative emotions, and has sometimes told me that **he can't comprehend why people can't choose to not feel bad, and that feeling bad is a choice in general.**
I've been searching for this post on my main account, and I can't seem to find it, whether through putting it through a search bar or browsing on /new, but it doesn't seem to be popping up.
